title: Gmail for bookkeepers on Mac: templates, filters and labels for client mail in a browser
metaTitle: Gmail for Bookkeepers on Mac: Templates, Filters and Labels
description: Gmail for bookkeepers on Mac, step by step: templates, filters, labels and delegate access, plus how Lazur helps you draft and dictate client emails.
intro: Gmail for bookkeepers on Mac runs in a browser, usually Safari or Chrome. Turn on templates, then set up filters and labels so client mail sorts itself. Lazur, a voice assistant for the Mac, can point at the control you need, guide you through a setting, and type a draft when you ask.
tldr: Google's help pages describe no native Gmail app for Mac, so most bookkeepers use Gmail in Safari or Chrome.
Templates handle the monthly summaries and alerts. Filters and labels sort the client mail that comes in.
Templates work only on a computer, and a deleted template cannot be recovered.
Delegation lets another person act inside one Gmail account. It is not a shared inbox.
Lazur helps you find things, learn steps, and type drafts. It does not click buttons for you.

blocks.text: Google's help pages describe no native Gmail app for Mac. So you open Gmail in a browser, pin it to the Dock as a Safari web app, or add your Gmail account to Apple's Mail app. All three read the same mail. The templates, filters, and labels on this page live inside Gmail, so set them up in the browser.
Which Gmail setup to use on your Mac
Start with Gmail in Safari or Chrome. It has every Gmail setting, including templates and filters. The other options work well for reading and replying. Setup still sends you back to the browser.

rows: The default choice. Every Gmail setting is here.
Same Gmail. Use a separate Chrome profile for client work.
Open Gmail in Safari, then choose File > Add to Dock
Needs macOS Sonoma 14 or later. Shares no history or cookies with Safari.
Mail > Add Account, then enter your Gmail address
Reads your mail. Set up templates and filters in Gmail on a computer.
blocks.caption: Four ways to open Gmail on a Mac, and what each one means for setup.

blocks.text: The Safari web app is handy for a Gmail window that stays open. It keeps its own sign-in. Apple says it shares no browsing history, cookies, website data, or settings with Safari. If it asks you to sign in again, that is expected. Keep the browser version for setup work.
What bookkeepers send in Gmail every month

Most client email falls into four types. Figurenote's bookkeeper guide lists monthly financial summaries, short issue alerts, annual review setup emails, and occasional check-ins. Count your own mail for one month. You will likely find the same four, sent again and again to different people.

items: Monthly financial summary, sent within five business days of close.
Short issue alert, when a bank feed breaks or a receipt is missing.
Annual review setup email, usually sent in November or December.
Occasional check-in, when a number looks odd and the client should know.

blocks.text: Gmail templates for summaries and alerts

Templates are the built-in way to reuse these messages. Gmail templates work only on a computer. You cannot create or use them in the mobile apps. Turn them on first under Settings > See all settings > Advanced > Templates.

items: Write the message once in Compose, with placeholders like [Client] and [Month].
Click More options, the three dots at the bottom of the compose window.
Choose Templates, then Save draft as template, then Save as new template.
To use it later, open Compose, go to More options > Templates, and pick it under Insert template.
Fill in the placeholders, read every figure, then send.

blocks.text: Here is a starting point. The subject line is adapted from the format in Figurenote's guide: [Month] Financial Summary, [Client Name]. The body reads: Hi [First name], your [Month] summary is attached. Cash is [up or down] by [amount] from last month. Two items need your reply by [date]. Thanks, [Your name].

blocks.title: Deleting a template is permanent
blocks.text: Gmail's template page says you cannot recover a deleted template. Before you overwrite one, open it in Compose and save a copy as a new template. Then edit the copy, not the original.

Templates fail in one common way. The same subject line goes out every month, and clients stop opening it. Change the month. Name one or two specific items in the first line, so the client knows why you are writing.
Gmail filters that sort client mail for you

A filter checks each new message as it arrives. Gmail can label, archive, delete, star, or forward mail that matches. Most bookkeepers label the mail and archive it, so it skips the inbox and waits in its folder. Filters only act on new mail, so plan for the backlog too.

items: Click the arrow at the right end of the search bar to show search options.
Enter your criteria, such as the client's sender address in the From box.
Click Search to preview which messages match.
Click Create filter, then choose the action, such as applying a label and archiving.
Click Create filter again to save it.

blocks.text: Say a client sends payroll reports from payroll@clientco.example. Search for from:payroll@clientco.example and check the preview. Then create a filter that applies a label called Clients/Clientco and archives the message. Every future report lands in one folder, and you open it when you need it.

Forwarding filters have one edge case. They only affect new messages. A filter that forwards to a teammate will not forward last quarter's mail. For older mail, search for it and apply a label in batches. The step-by-step filter guide is at [how to create a filter in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail).
Labels for each client, and the limits to know

Labels let you find a client's mail in one click. Gmail allows up to 5,000 labels and up to 100 custom label colors. Create a label with the control next to Labels in the sidebar. Check Nest label under to place it inside another label, such as Clients > Clientco > 2026. Google's Workspace guidance suggests 500 labels or fewer, including nested labels. Keep the tree shallow.

rows: More than a practice needs. Clutter is the real risk.
Color each client group so the sidebar scans fast.
Use one label per client, then years only where needed.
Select in batches when you label, archive, or delete.
Matters for very large Workspace inboxes only.
blocks.caption: Limits from Google's Gmail Help and Workspace admin guidance.

blocks.text: Watch for labels that grow too deep. A label path like 2026 > January > Clientco > Invoices is four levels deep. Search can find it, but you will stop using it. Two levels are usually enough for a bookkeeping practice.
Sharing access with a bookkeeping partner

Delegation lets another person work in your Gmail account. A personal @gmail.com account can add up to 10 delegates. A work or school account can add up to 1,000. A delegate can read, send, and delete emails in the account. Delegates cannot chat or change the password. You cannot add delegates from the Gmail app, so use a computer.

items: Delegation is tied to one Google Account. It is not a shared inbox for your whole team.
Google's page covers that account only. It does not cover aliases or alternate addresses.
A delegate can delete mail, so give access only to someone you trust with the account.
Remove access when a person stops working with you. Check the delegate list each quarter.

blocks.text: Set this up before tax season, not during it. The setup itself is quick. Step-by-step instructions are at [how to give delegate access in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/give-someone-access-to-your-mailbox-in-gmail).
Where Lazur helps inside Gmail on your Mac

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. It is not a plugin or add-in for Gmail. It does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where Templates is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to create a filter, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Dictation is the other half. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app, including the Gmail compose window. Snippets save phrases you repeat, such as your sign-off. The personal dictionary keeps client names and account terms spelled right. Clipboard slots hold text you need to paste twice.

Privacy matters here. Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. A Gmail window can still show bank details and payroll figures. Check your firm's rules before you ask about a screen that shows client account data.
Worked example: answering a client about a missing statement
Say a dental practice client has not sent the March bank statement, and your reply is due Friday. Here is how that looks with Lazur on your Mac.

items: Open the thread in Gmail. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask what the client is asking for. Lazur answers out loud.
Click Reply. Hold fn and dictate the opening line, including the month and the missing account.
Ask Lazur to draft the rest in a plain, polite tone. It types the draft at your cursor.
Read every figure yourself. Change any number that does not match your books.
Press ⌘ Return to send. Lazur does not send the email for you.

blocks.text: The draft is the fast part. Checking is the part that matters in bookkeeping. A dictated line can get an account name or a date wrong. Read the whole reply again before you send it.
Mistakes bookkeepers make with Gmail on Mac

items: Sending a template with last month's numbers. Read the summary once before you send.
Expecting a forwarding filter to move old mail. It only affects new messages.
Selecting 1,000 or more messages at once. Google's guidance is to stay under 1,000.
Building a label tree four levels deep. Two levels is usually enough.
Sharing one login across the practice. Delegation is set per account, so each person needs their own access.
Expecting a Safari web app to share your Safari sign-in. It keeps its own.
Trusting a figure without checking its source. Vendor time savings are often guesses.

blocks.text: How much time email takes bookkeepers each week

The best measured figure comes from a 2024 survey of 240 accounting professionals. CPA Practice Advisor published it, and Canopy co-sponsored it. Respondents spent 9.3 hours a week on client communication. Email took 35.4% of that time. The survey was fielded in June 2024. It covers accounting professionals, not bookkeepers.

Research turned up no measured study of bookkeepers' Gmail time. Vendor examples are not measurements. Getpoint's example of 11.5 hours dropping to 5.5 hours uses fourteen clients, and Getpoint calls it hypothetical. Figurenote says a 25-minute email drops to 5 minutes with a template, but gives no basis for that figure.
Test the numbers on your own week instead. For two weeks, log each client email, the minutes it took, and whether a template would fit. That log shows which template to build first.
A simple first week with Gmail on your Mac

items: Open Gmail in Safari or Chrome, then turn on Templates under Settings > See all settings > Advanced > Templates.
Write your monthly summary once and save it as a template.
Create one label for each client, nested by year only where you need it.
Make one filter for your biggest client sender, and preview it before you save.
Draft or dictate two replies with Lazur, then read every figure before you send.

blocks.text: Add the next template or filter only after the first one works. Change one thing at a time, so you know what caused a problem. The [Gmail for bookkeepers page](/for/bookkeepers) covers the wider set of tools. When you are ready, [download Lazur](/download) and try the hold-to-ask shortcut on this page.

blocks.title: Check the menu names on your screen
blocks.text: Gmail changes its menu wording from time to time. If a label on your screen differs from this page, check Google's Gmail Help pages, which are the final word.

faq.question: Is there a native Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: Google's help pages describe no native Gmail app for Mac. Most bookkeepers use Gmail in Safari or Chrome. You can also add Gmail to the Dock as a Safari web app, which needs macOS Sonoma 14 or later.

faq.question: Can I use Gmail templates on my iPhone?
faq.answer: No. Google says templates can only be turned on and used from Gmail on a computer, not in the mobile apps. Create and use them on your Mac.

faq.question: Do Gmail forwarding filters move old emails too?
faq.answer: No. Forwarding filters only affect new messages. For older mail, search for it and apply a label in batches of fewer than 1,000 messages.

faq.question: Can my bookkeeping partner read and send from my Gmail?
faq.answer: Yes, through delegation. A personal account can add up to 10 delegates, and a work or school account up to 1,000. A delegate can read, send, and delete, but cannot chat or change the password. It is not a shared inbox.

faq.question: Does Lazur read my Gmail or send emails for me?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. It answers, points, guides, and types drafts. It does not click buttons, so you send each email yourself. Audio and screenshots go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows too?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned but not available yet.

faq.question: Is there a free trial?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur has a free trial that does not ask for a credit card. See the [pricing page](/pricing) for current terms.

faq.question: What if the menu names on my screen are different?
faq.answer: Gmail changes its wording sometimes. Use the steps here as a guide, then check Google's Gmail Help pages. You can also ask Lazur to point at the control you want, and it draws a circle around it.
